chief_complaint: central facial redness and pimples triggered by coffee
hpi_details: A 32-year-old female presents to the clinic with central facial redness and pimples triggered by coffee. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: thinks it might be related to rosacea
concerns: worried about potential complications and long term recovery
expectations: wants complete diagnostic evaluation and treatment plan

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Papulopustular Rosacea is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Papulopustular Rosacea: Avoid triggers, sunscreen daily, topical Metronidazole 0.75% gel, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Papulopustular Rosacea.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Acne vulgaris without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Ocular symptoms (dryness, redness, foreign-body sensation, blurred vision) — ocular rosacea can threaten vision and needs ophthalmology referral.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: central facial redness and pimples triggered by coffee

A 32-year-old female presents with central facial erythema and inflammatory papules/pustules that flare after drinking coffee, gradually worsening over time.
reference_soap.objective: Central facial erythema with telangiectasias and scattered inflammatory papules/pustules over the cheeks, nose, and chin. No comedones present. No ocular involvement noted.
reference_soap.plan: Plan for Papulopustular Rosacea: Avoid triggers, sunscreen daily, topical Metronidazole 0.75% gel. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Papulopustular Rosacea
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Papulopustular Rosacea
Implement evidence-based management plan: Avoid triggers, sunscreen daily, topical Metronidazole 0.75% gel

teaching.one_liner: Central facial redness and pimples triggered by common dietary and environmental factors like coffee.
red_flags: Ocular symptoms (dryness, redness, foreign-body sensation, blurred vision) — ocular rosacea can threaten vision and needs ophthalmology referral
Progressive skin thickening of the nose (rhinophyma) — needs specialist referral
Sudden severe flushing episodes with other systemic symptoms (diarrhea, wheezing) — consider a secondary cause such as carcinoid syndrome

must_ask.say: Are there pimples along with the redness?
How long has this been going on?
Have you tried anything for it?
